title: Search on the answer
summary: When you can check whether a guess works, and every bigger guess works too, binary search the guesses instead of the data.
idea: If “does x work?” is false then true as x grows, the smallest x that works is a boundary. Binary search finds it in log(range) checks.

signals.see: The question asks for the minimum or maximum value of a setting: speed, capacity, size, or time.
signals.think: Search over that setting, not over the input. Each guess becomes a yes/no check.

signals.see: Given a guess, you can check it greedily in one pass.
signals.think: Write can(x) first. If it is monotone (once true, always true), binary search x.

signals.see: The answer lies in a known range, such as 1 to the largest input.
signals.think: Set lo and hi to that range. It can be far larger than n and still only cost log steps.

signals.see: Phrases like “minimise the largest” or “maximise the smallest”.
signals.think: Guess the limit, check whether it is achievable, and move toward the best limit that works.

phrasings: A courier must deliver parcels in order within d days. What is the smallest van capacity that works?
Cut ribbons into k pieces of equal length. What is the longest length possible?
Split a reading list into m days so the busiest day is as light as possible.

picture.title: Search the answers, not the data
picture.alt: On the left, every speed from 1 upward is tried, with a full check each time. On the right, the range of speeds is halved using the check, so only about log of the range checks run.
picture.caption: The check costs O(n). Binary search runs it only log(range) times.

code.py:
def min_speed(piles, hours):
    lo, hi = 1, max(piles)  #@init
    while lo < hi:  #@loop
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2  #@mid
        need = sum((p + mid - 1) // mid for p in piles)  #@need
        if need <= hours: hi = mid  #@fits
        else: lo = mid + 1  #@slow
    return lo  #@done

visualiser.inputHelp: Up to 8 pile sizes from 1 to 15, separated by commas. Hours is from 1 to 40 and at least the number of piles.

oneLiner: lo, hi = smallest, largest answer; works(mid) → hi = mid, else lo = mid + 1; return lo

exercise.prompt: lengths are rope lengths. You want at least k pieces that all have the same whole-number length L, cut from the ropes (leftovers are wasted). Return the largest L that works, or 0 if even L = 1 gives fewer than k pieces. The starter never moves lo up when a guess works. Fix the search. Note: mid is rounded up so lo = mid always makes progress.

starter.py:
def longest_piece(lengths, k):
    lo, hi = 0, max(lengths, default=0)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        pieces = sum(length // mid for length in lengths)
        # If mid gives at least k pieces, keep it: move lo up. Otherwise move hi down.
        hi = mid - 1
    return lo

hints: More length means fewer pieces, so “gives at least k pieces” is true for small L and false for big L. You want the last true.
If pieces >= k, set lo = mid (mid works, maybe bigger does too). Otherwise set hi = mid - 1.

complexity.why: R is the size of the answer range, such as the largest pile. Binary search runs about log₂ R checks, and each check is one O(n) pass.

mistakes: Searching over the input positions instead of over the possible answers.
Using a check that is not monotone. If a bigger guess can fail after a smaller one works, binary search is wrong.
Setting lo = mid with mid rounded down, which loops forever. Round up when you move lo to mid.
Choosing a range that misses the answer, such as starting lo at 0 and then dividing by mid.
Integer overflow in other languages when adding large counts. Stop the check early once it is over the limit.

quiz.question: What must be true of works(x) for search on the answer to be correct?
choices: Once it is true for some x, it stays true for every bigger x
It is true for exactly one x
quiz.explain: Binary search needs one flip from false to true. Then the smallest x that works is a boundary you can halve toward.

quiz.question: You want the largest L that works and you set lo = mid when mid works. How should mid be computed?
quiz.explain: Rounding up makes mid > lo whenever lo < hi, so lo = mid always shrinks the range.

quiz.question: Piles are up to 10⁹ in size and there are n piles. How many checks does the search make?
quiz.explain: log₂(10⁹) is about 30. Each check is O(n), so the total is about 30n.

interviewTip: Write and test the check function first, then say “this check is monotone, so I can binary search the answer”. That sentence shows you know why the method works.
